items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: Archie Blyar was very good. Some of them were a little far out, but after you wait them out, they got all right.

ctx.x: They have a lot of Warrington arrangements here. Yeah, yeah. He was very good. Did you ever play any Archie Blyar arrangements? Yes, very good.

Now you're bringing them back. Archie Blyar was very good. Some of them were a little far out, but after you wait them out, they got all right. You know what I mean? You didn't always have men that could. But the trouble is why I tricked them, I'll tell you why. Because if you put a curtain in front of the bands they all sound alike. You know what I mean? If I played the Stock of the Song from beginning to end of Blue Moon, and that other band plays it, you wouldn't know what band it was then. So I tricked them.…
Did you have any favorite popular composers, let's say when you started out, say in the twenties, people that were, stick out in their minds?
